questions.question: What does 'a brand' actually refer to in this course?
questions.questionHtml: What does 'a brand' actually refer to in this course?

answers.text: A logo and colour palette
The consistent promise and feeling customers can expect across every interaction
answers.textHtml: The consistent promise and feeling customers can expect across every interaction

answers.text: Your registered LLC name
Your social media follower count

questions.feedback: A brand is a consistent promise and feeling. The logo is one of many ways that promise gets transmitted, but the brand itself is something larger.
questions.feedbackHtml: A brand is the consistent promise and feeling — the visuals are how it is transmitted.

questions.question: In what order should the three layers of a brand be built?
questions.questionHtml: In what order should the three layers of a brand be built?

answers.text: Visuals → Voice → Core
Core → Voice → Visuals
Voice → Visuals → Core
Visuals → Core → Voice

questions.feedback: Decide who you are and how you sound first. The visuals will then practically design themselves. Most operators get this backwards.
questions.feedbackHtml: Build inside-out: core, then voice, then visuals.

questions.question: Why should drone operators apply a consistent colour grade or LUT to all video?
questions.questionHtml: Why should drone operators apply a consistent colour grade or LUT to all video?

answers.text: Because the FAA requires colour-correct footage
Because consistent grading makes your work recognisable in a feed before viewers see your name
answers.textHtml: Because consistent grading makes your work recognisable in a feed before viewers see your name

answers.text: Because it speeds up rendering
Because clients explicitly ask for it

questions.feedback: A consistent colour grade is the visual fingerprint of a drone brand. People recognise it subconsciously while scrolling, even before they read the caption or see the logo.
questions.feedbackHtml: Consistent grading is what makes your work recognisable in the feed.

questions.question: What is the goal of positioning?

answers.text: To be the cheapest option in your area
answers.textHtml: To be the cheapest option in your area

answers.text: To rank first on Google
To become the obvious choice in a customer's mind for a specific kind of need
answers.textHtml: To become the obvious choice in a customer's mind for a specific kind of need

answers.text: To have the most followers on Instagram
answers.textHtml: To have the most followers on Instagram

questions.feedback: Positioning is about being the most obvious choice for a specific customer with a specific need — not about being the best, cheapest, or most-followed.
questions.feedbackHtml: Positioning aims to make you the obvious choice for a specific need.
